current_policy_status.current_london_plan: London Plan 2021 remains the current statutory planning framework
current_policy_status.draft_next_london_plan: Draft next London Plan is under consultation in 2026 and is not adopted
current_policy_status.support_for_housebuilding_lpg: Published/adopted in March 2026 as time-limited guidance; material consideration, not itself the statutory development plan
current_policy_status.london_infrastructure_framework: Published March 2026 as strategic infrastructure delivery framework

batches.title: Opportunity Area boundary/status gate
batches.coverage: Opportunity Area evidence is strategic growth context. Adopted, emerging and boundary-to-be-defined states must remain distinct; only an exact candidate-to-boundary relationship can promote an OA signal.

batches.title: Opportunity Area capacity/infrastructure gate
batches.coverage: OA homes/jobs capacities are strategic starting points and depend on infrastructure and local planning. Capacity figures are not parcel capacity without exact boundary/site and delivery evidence.

batches.title: Town-centre network/intensification gate
batches.coverage: London Plan town-centre policy supports sustainable intensification, but candidate use requires exact centre/boundary and current local-plan relationship; London-wide town-centre policy is not parcel allocation.

batches.title: Strategic Industrial Location designation gate
batches.coverage: Strategic Industrial Locations protect and manage major industrial capacity. Candidate impact requires exact SIL boundary/designation and current local-plan implementation; London-wide listing alone is insufficient.

batches.title: Industrial intensification/co-location gate
batches.coverage: Industrial intensification and co-location policies are proposal- and site-specific. Exact industrial designation, replacement capacity and proposal facts are required before candidate scoring.

batches.title: Affordable-housing threshold/viability gate
batches.coverage: Affordable-housing thresholds depend on proposal type, land status, tenure and viability route. The 2026 support-for-housebuilding route is time-limited guidance and must not be treated as a parcel attribute.

batches.title: Housing supply/design-led site-capacity gate
batches.coverage: London Plan housing supply and design-led capacity policies guide plan-making and proposals. Candidate capacity requires exact site constraints, local allocations and design assumptions.

batches.title: Housing design/2026 housebuilding-guidance status gate
batches.coverage: Housing Design Standards remain adopted guidance while 2026 Support for Housebuilding LPG introduces time-limited changes. Guidance status/effectivity must be read before applying proposal requirements.

batches.title: Tall-building location/suitability gate
batches.coverage: Policy D9 requires suitable tall-building locations and heights to be identified in Development Plans. A London-wide tall-building policy cannot establish candidate suitability without local mapped policy and proposal height.

batches.title: Public London Charter/public-realm gate
batches.coverage: The Public London Charter applies where development provides new public space and requires management commitments. It is proposal-specific, not an existing parcel constraint.

batches.title: Social-infrastructure need/capacity gate
batches.coverage: Social-infrastructure policy relies on local needs assessment, accessibility and delivery. London-wide policy cannot prove that a candidate has spare school/health/community capacity.

batches.title: Air Quality Neutral proposal gate
batches.coverage: Air Quality Neutral guidance sets benchmarks for development emissions. Candidate effect requires proposal scale/use, transport/building emissions and local air-quality context; it is not a parcel score.

batches.title: Urban Greening Factor proposal gate
batches.coverage: UGF is a development-design metric. It requires proposal surface-cover information and applicable local/London target; no UGF score can be inferred from a parcel coordinate alone.

batches.title: Biodiversity Net Gain/nature gate
batches.coverage: BNG requires habitat baseline, statutory metric and planning-authority implementation. London biodiversity policy and design guidance do not supply a candidate BNG result without site habitat evidence.

batches.title: Green Belt/Metropolitan Open Land gate
batches.coverage: Green Belt and Metropolitan Open Land have strong strategic protection. Candidate effect requires exact current boundary intersection and relevant local-plan evidence; illustrative London maps are not parcel proof.

batches.title: Flood-risk/sustainable-drainage gate
batches.coverage: Flood and SuDS strategy is spatial and proposal-specific. Candidate scoring requires exact current flood-risk/drainage catchment evidence and proposal drainage facts; strategic strategy alone is insufficient.

batches.title: Energy-infrastructure capacity gate
batches.coverage: Energy infrastructure policy requires network capacity and proposal demand evidence. Strategic policy does not prove electrical/energy capacity at a candidate site.

batches.title: Heat-risk/heat-network opportunity gate
batches.coverage: Heat-network mapping identifies existing/proposed networks and opportunities; proposed networks are not operational capacity. Candidate use requires exact network proximity/connection feasibility and proposal heat demand.

batches.title: Be Seen operational-energy monitoring gate
batches.coverage: Be Seen is an adopted monitoring requirement for major development. It applies through proposal/permission obligations and cannot be converted into an existing parcel score.

batches.title: Whole-life carbon assessment gate
batches.coverage: WLC assessment requirements depend on proposal type and design/material assumptions. No site WLC outcome exists until a qualifying development proposal and assessment are available.

batches.title: Circular-economy statement gate
batches.coverage: Circular Economy Statement requirements concern design, construction, reuse and waste commitments for qualifying proposals. They are not an inherent parcel attribute.

batches.title: Water-infrastructure/waterways gate
batches.coverage: Water infrastructure and waterways policies require local capacity, flood/drainage and waterway relationship evidence. London-wide policy is not parcel-level capacity or constraint proof.

batches.title: Digital-connectivity infrastructure gate
batches.coverage: Digital-connectivity policy requires current network/service and proposal requirements. Strategic infrastructure need cannot establish candidate service capacity without provider/location evidence.

batches.title: London Infrastructure Framework 2026 delivery gate
batches.coverage: The March 2026 London Infrastructure Framework is a strategic long-term delivery framework across transport, energy, water, waste and digital systems. It does not itself prove parcel infrastructure availability.

batches.title: TfL WebCAT/PTAL accessibility gate
batches.coverage: WebCAT is a strategic connectivity assessment tool and explicitly is not a journey planner or necessarily current travel conditions. Candidate accessibility requires exact location, selected scenario/year and network assumptions.

batches.title: Transport capacity/Healthy Streets/cycling-parking gate
batches.coverage: Transport assessments, Healthy Streets, cycling, parking, servicing and mitigation are proposal-specific. Strategic transport policy cannot be converted to parcel capacity without network and proposal analysis.

batches.title: Heritage/strategic-views/LVMF gate
batches.coverage: London heritage and strategic-view policies require exact asset, setting, assessment point or protected-vista relationship. Illustrative maps and city-wide heritage counts are not parcel proof.

batches.title: Waste-capacity/safeguarded-site/aggregates gate
batches.coverage: London Plan waste and aggregates policies manage strategic capacity and safeguarded sites. Candidate impact requires exact safeguarded-site/mineral relationship and current local implementation.
